chapter: West Coast trip and Mildred's circle
title: Whiteman drives to Mildred's house and hires her
summary: Bing and Al praised Mildred to Whiteman and his band, so Whiteman knocked on her door in California and hired her for the Old Gold program.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: -- now here's the connection between Whiteman, now -- Bing and Al used to talk about how great Mildred sang.
-- so when Paul went to the Coast, to do King of Jazz, he heard so much about her, see, and some of the guys in the Whiteman band had heard her sing and at a party --
And they were knocked out with Mildred's singing.
And there were no women that could ever sing jazz, then.
NO, no. Nobody had a feel -- and understanding -- in those days, they used to tell me that they'd never heard -- the guys in the band, musicians --
Frankie Trumbauer, said, She's the first singer that I ever heard that I could understand every word she said and understand where it made sense to me.
-- she made a happy marriage between the lyrics and the music.
And she set -- the -- she was unlimited as to what liberties she could take, but she never overdid it, really.
So finally Whiteman heard so many he just got in his car one day and drove out and knocked on the door, and said, 'All right, I been hearing about you, let me hear you sing now.'
Went to her house in California.

So they called up Al and then they came over and -- and the way I understand it, she was making beer for Whiteman -- she made beer and everything, so she opened a bottle of beer and they waited till Al and them got there, and they started and that's when she -- he hired her to go on the Old Gold program.
Oh, yeah, she went right on.
